block.jev.model.description: Evaluates text or JSON with TypeSafe Jev and returns typed answers with probabilities.
block.jev.title: Block name
block.jev.key_hint: Store your TypeSafe API key in the wallet. Enter only its reference here, never the key.
block.jev.model_hint: jev-latest follows stable releases. Enter a versioned Jev ID to pin the model.
block.jev.flow_hint: Connect text or JSON to state. All questions run in one request. result contains the model, typed answers, probabilities and token usage.
block.jev.privacy: Each execution sends the state and questions to TypeSafe, including in One Shot Simulation. Jev judges data; it does not generate prose or execute code.
block.jev.limits_hint: Retries apply only to HTTP 429/529, within the total timeout. Network failures are not retried. Provider token limits still apply.
block.jev.questions_hint: Ask one clear judgment per question. Questions are independent: they cannot see each other’s answers. Their IDs are for your workflow, not instructions to Jev.
block.jev.json_editor: Advanced: edit all questions as JSON
block.jev.json_hint: Structured instructions and criteria (objects or arrays) are supported. Changes here update the question cards when you leave the editor.
block.jev.noul_hint: Optional: {"true":"What counts as yes","false":"What counts as no"}. The answer is P(yes), not intensity.
block.jev.choice_hint: Object with 2–255 named options and descriptions (or null). Include other when no option may fit.
block.jev.score_hint: Array of 2–10 concrete, ordered levels. The score runs from 0 to the last level’s index.
block.jev.invalid_questions: Check the JSON, unique identifiers and required instructions. At least one question is required.
block.jev.questions_valid: Draft ready. Apply to save these questions.
block.jev.apply_hint: Changes remain local until you apply them.
